newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - April 7.

text.p: Following were the leading stories in Sri Lankan newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Sri Lanka's first coal-fired power plant with initial capacity of 300 MW to be located in the Puttalam district north of Colombo.

Sri Lanka Buddhist Congress and many Hindu and Christian religious bodies welcome move by President Kumaratunga and main opposition United National Party (UNP) leader Ranil Wickremesinghe to adopt bipartisan approach in solving northeast conflict.

Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar to brief Indian leaders on agreement between President Kumaratunga and opposition leader, during his visit to New Delhi to attend a ministerial meeting of the Non-Aligned Movement.
A woman lecturer at southern Ruhunu University and her six-year-old son commit suicide by consuming cynide.
The UNP will participate in finding a solution to the ethnic conflict without seeking to score political points, says party leader Ranil Wickremesinghe.

There is no truth in rumours that government is preparing to launch peace talks with the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels or seek third party mediation to end the ethnic war, Foreign Minister Lakshman Kadirgamar says.
